subject: [Auto-Acknowledgement] Singapore Arrival Card (SGAC) - Acknowledgement of Arrival Information & Health Declaration submission

parts.body:
Dear TEST ONE,

Thank you for your submission of the Singapore Arrival Card (SGAC) to the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) on 09/09/2026 17:30 (Singapore Time). We have received your submission.


DO NOTE THAT

  • The making of false or misleading health and/or travel declaration is an offence under Singapore law.

  • If you wish to make any change in your health status or arrival information prior to your arrival in Singapore, you may retrieve and update your declaration via the SGAC e-Service or MyICA mobile application with your Disembarkation/Embarkation (DE) Number: X8276T7137.

DECLARATION DETAILS


Disembarkation/Embarkation (DE) Number X8276T7137
Full Name (In Passport) TEST ONE
Passport Number T11949149
Mobile Number 93111441555
Email Address SGAC-FORE@TEAM380551.TESTINATOR.EMAIL
Accommodation TRANSIT
Date of Arrival (DD/MM/YYYY) 09/09/2026
Purpose of Travel Education/Training
Do you currently have fever, cough, shortness of breath, headache, vomiting, dizziness or rash? NO
Have you visited any of the listed countries^ in Africa or Latin America in the past 6 days prior to your arrival in Singapore? NO

This SG Arrival Card is only valid for one time use on the expected date of your arrival in Singapore indicated above. The use of the SG Arrival Card e-Service is free of charge. Please note that the SG Arrival Card is not a visa. For more information regarding entry visa requirements, please refer to ICA's website.

Thank you for using the SG Arrival Card! We wish you a pleasant visit to Singapore.

Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA)
Website: www.ica.gov.sg
Facebook: fb.com/Immigration.Checkpoints.Authority

Contact Us

This is a system-generated email. Please do not reply to this email address.


IMPORTANT NOTICE

  1. The unauthorised consumption, possession, import, export and/or trafficking of any controlled drug is an offence under Singapore's Misuse of Drugs Act. Under the Misuse of Drugs Act, drug trafficking is punishable by death.

  2. Vaping is an offence which carries fines of up to $2,000 and rehabilitation. Repeat offenders of etomidate vapes will face up to a 12-month regime, including detention at Drug Rehabilitation Centre followed by mandatory supervision. Importers, sellers and distributors of etomidate vapes will face up to 20 years’ imprisonment and 15 strokes of the cane. Foreigners caught vaping may have their passes revoked, be deported and banned from re-entry into Singapore.

  3. If you make any false or misleading health and/or travel declaration, you may be prosecuted for an offence(s) under Singapore law, including under the Infectious Diseases Act. If found guilty, you shall be liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding S$10,000 or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 6 months or to both for first offence; or to a fine not exceeding S$20,000 or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months or to both for subsequent offence.

  4. If you are entering or leaving Singapore carrying a total value of Physical Currency and Bearer Negotiable Instruments (CBNI) exceeding S$20,000 (or its equivalent in a foreign currency), please submit a cash (CBNI) declaration.

  5. If you are bringing in any item, or carrying an item for someone, but you do not know what it contains, you must declare the item at the Red Channel.

  6. All arriving travellers are required to declare and pay the duty and Goods and Services Tax (GST) on all dutiable and taxable goods exceeding their duty-free concession and GST relief. For your convenience, do make use of the Customs@SG web application to make an advance declaration and tax payment prior to your arrival in Singapore. Please refer to Customs website for more information.

You can refer to the ICA website at "Entering, Transiting and Departing Singapore" for more information on Singapore's entry requirements and the list of prohibited or controlled items.


Government officials will NEVER ask you to transfer money or disclose bank log-in details over a phone call. Call the 24/7 ScamShield Helpline at 1799 if you are unsure if something is a scam.
